Consider the following initial value problem: y′=x2−y2,y(0)=1 Using the implicit Euler method with step size Δx=0.25, the new value ynew is obtained by solving the equation g(ynew)=0 at each step. Which of the following is the general form of g(ynew) in terms of the new values xnew and ynew, and the current value y?

a
g(ynew)=0.25(xnew)2−ynew+y−0.25y2
b
g(ynew)=0.25(ynew)2−ynew+y−0.25(xnew)2
c
g(ynew)=ynew−y−0.25(xnew)2−0.25(ynew)2
d
g(ynew)=0.25(ynew)2+ynew−y−0.25(xnew)2
e
g(ynew)=0.25y2+ynew−y−0.25(xnew)2
Submit

decision.explanation: Implicit Euler evaluates the derivative at the new point: y_new = y + 0.25(x_new^2 − y_new^2). Moving all terms to the left gives g(y_new) = 0.25y_new^2 + y_new − y − 0.25x_new^2, which is option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,y(0)=1
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=0.25,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current value $y?$
after.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2})\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2} \\ {{0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.25$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}.
$$

$$

Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current value $y?$
content.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2})\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2} \\ {{0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.25$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}.
$$

Question 2
?

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=xy−y2,y(0)=2 Using the implicit Euler method with step size Δx=0.25, the new value ynew is obtained by solving the equation g(ynew)=0 at each step. Which of the following is the general form of g(ynew) in terms of the new values xnew and ynew, and the current value y?

a
g(ynew)=0.25y2+ynew−0.25xnewynew−y
b
g(ynew)=ynew−y−0.25xnewynew−0.25(ynew)2
c
g(ynew)=0.25(ynew)2−ynew+0.25xnewynew−y
d
g(ynew)=0.25(ynew)2+ynew−0.25xnewynew−y
e
g(ynew)=0.25xnewynew−ynew+y−0.25y2
Submit

decision.explanation: Implicit Euler gives y_new = y + 0.25(x_new y_new − y_new²). Moving all terms to the left gives g(y_new) = 0.25y_new² + y_new − 0.25x_new y_new − y, matching option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x\,y-{y}^{2},\,y(0)=2
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=0.25,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current value $y?$
after.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =({x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2})\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side to define $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2} \\ {{0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-y}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.25$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-y.
$$

Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x\,y-{y}^{2},\,y(0)=2
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=0.25,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current value $y?$
content.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =({x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2})\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side to define $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2} \\ {{0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-y}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.25$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-y.
$$

Question 3

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=y2+x,y(0)=2 Using the implicit Euler method with step size Δx=1, the new value ynew is obtained by solving the equation g(ynew)=0 at each step. Which of the following is the specific function g(ynew) used in the first step?

a
g(ynew)=ynew−(ynew)2−xnew
b
g(ynew)=(ynew)2−ynew−3
c
g(ynew)=ynew−(ynew)2+3
d
g(ynew)=ynew−(ynew)2−3
e
g(ynew)=(ynew)2+ynew+3
Submit

decision.explanation: In the first step, x_new = 1 and the current y = 2. Implicit Euler gives y_new = 2 + (y_new² + 1), so g(y_new) = y_new − y_new² − 3, matching option d. This equation has no real root, but the requested function is still well-defined.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}+x,\,y(0)=2
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=1,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **specific function** $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ used in the first step?
after.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}})\cdot 1 \\  & =({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}} \\ {{{y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-y-{x}_{\text{new}}}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=1$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-y-{x}_{\text{new}}.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0+1=1.$ Therefore, the function used in the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-2-1 \\  & ={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=y2+x,y(0)=2 Using the implicit Euler method with step size Δx=1, the new value ynew is obtained by solving the equation g(ynew)=0 at each step. Which of the following is the specific function g(ynew) used in the first step?

a
g(ynew)=ynew−(ynew)2−xnew
b
g(ynew)=(ynew)2−ynew−3
c
g(ynew)=ynew−(ynew)2+3
d
g(ynew)=ynew−(ynew)2−3
e
g(ynew)=(ynew)2+ynew+3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y0=y(x0), the implicit Euler method with step size Δx is given by Δy=ynew′⋅Δx, with ynew′=f(xnew,ynew) evaluated at the next x and y values.

In general, Δy is given by

Δy=ynew′⋅Δx=((ynew)2+xnew)⋅1=(ynew)2+xnew.

We substitute this into ynew=y+Δy and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as g(ynew):

ynew=y+Δyynew=y+(ynew)2+xnewynew−(ynew)2−y−xnew⏟g(ynew)=0.

So, the general form of the function g for step size Δx=1 is

g(ynew)=ynew−(ynew)2−y−xnew.

Now, in the first step, the new x value is xnew=x+Δx=0+1=1. Therefore, the function used in the first step is

g(ynew)=ynew−(ynew)2−2−1=ynew−(ynew)2−3.

content.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}+x,\,y(0)=2
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=1,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **specific function** $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ used in the first step?
content.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}})\cdot 1 \\  & =({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}} \\ {{{y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-y-{x}_{\text{new}}}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=1$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-y-{x}_{\text{new}}.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0+1=1.$ Therefore, the function used in the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-2-1 \\  & ={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3.\end{aligned}
$$
